name: Mara
persona: Thirteen years of dance music, taken seriously and played loudly.
blurb: Dub techno, UK bass, jungle and ambient, with a record collector's sense of where all of it came from. Long sessions, low skips, and one lane that burned out completely in June.

lanes.name: Dub Chamber
lanes.description: Dub techno and deep minimal: reverb as an instrument, chords used like weather.
lanes.arc: The steadiest room in the record all thirteen weeks, and the one the newer picks keep circling back to.

lanes.name: UK Bass
lanes.description: Bass music from the island: garage, dubstep's deeper end, and whatever Bristol is calling it now.
lanes.arc: Grew through early summer and now takes almost as much listening as the dub room.

lanes.name: Jungle & Drum and Bass
lanes.description: Breakbeat science from ninety-three onward, amen breaks and Metalheadz weight.
lanes.arc: Rising fast, mostly on the new jungle revival rather than the old records.

lanes.name: Electro & Braindance
lanes.description: Electro, Rephlex-adjacent melody and the machines that never sound quite human.
lanes.arc: Held steady, with the acid end getting more attention than the melodic end lately.

lanes.name: Ambient & Drone
lanes.description: Long-form ambient and drone: the records that get put on and left on.
lanes.arc: Grew quietly, mostly at night and mostly as a way to come down from the club records.

lanes.name: Deconstructed Club
lanes.description: Modern club music that has taken itself apart: unstable rhythm, no genre to sit in.
lanes.arc: The newest room and still filling, mostly from radio rather than from records.

lanes.name: House Lineage
lanes.description: House traced back through Chicago and Detroit, plus the deep end of the modern version.
lanes.arc: Reliable and unhurried, the lane that never spikes and never dips.

lanes.name: Hard Techno
lanes.description: The fast, loud, functional end: warehouse techno with nothing decorative left on it.
lanes.arc: Hammered through the spring and then dropped completely in June, which is the clearest break in the record.

lanes.name: Breaks & Hardcore
lanes.description: Hardcore continuum artefacts: breakbeat hardcore, rave stabs, happy accidents.
lanes.arc: Went quiet after February and has only been touched a handful of times since.

lanes.name: Dub & Roots
lanes.description: The Jamaican source: King Tubby's mixing desk and the records that took it seriously.
lanes.arc: A small, personal room that grows a little every month and never gets skipped.

issues.title: Chain Reaction
issues.dek: Thirteen weeks in and the dub room is still the centre of everything, so this week goes all the way in.

issues.title: Amen Corner
issues.dek: The jungle revival keeps getting better, and two of these came out this month.

issues.title: Grey Water
issues.dek: Bristol weight, mixed down until the low end is the only thing left.

issues.title: Machine Language
issues.dek: Electro from three continents, none of it trying to sound human.

issues.title: Left Hand Path
issues.dek: Deconstructed club and the sound of rhythm falling over on purpose.

issues.title: Warehouse Ghost
issues.dek: You stopped playing hard techno in June, so this is the version of it that survives.

issues.title: Deep Water Mark
issues.dek: Chicago and Detroit house, and the modern records that understood the assignment.

issues.title: Kingston Rules
issues.dek: Dub as an engineering practice, from the desk that invented it.

issues.title: Slow Pressure
issues.dek: An hour of ambient with a pulse in it, which is the only ambient you finish.

issues.title: Second Frequency
issues.dek: Half of last issue went unplayed, so this one is shorter and stranger.

issues.title: Rave Artefact
issues.dek: Hardcore fragments and the people still building out of them.

issues.title: Signal Chain
issues.dek: Records that sound like their own studio, from Basic Channel forward.

issues.title: Night Ferry
issues.dek: Closing the summer with the deep end of everything, and one record made in Iceland.

albums.title: See Mi Yah
albums.label: Burial Mix
albums.note: One rhythm, ten singers, no variation permitted, and it is completely hypnotic.

albums.title: In Full Effect
albums.label: Future Retro
albums.note: Modern jungle made with total conviction, no irony anywhere in it.

albums.title: Tessellations
albums.label: Punch Drunk
albums.note: Bristol techno built out of dubstep parts, and the drums never resolve where you expect.

albums.title: Gesamtkunstwerk
albums.label: Gigolo
albums.note: Electro delivered like a physics lecture, cold enough to be genuinely funny.

albums.title: Tumbling Towards a Wall
albums.label: Experiences Ltd
albums.note: Ambient made of fragments that never quite lock together, and better for the gaps.

albums.title: Cocoon Crush
albums.label: Pan
albums.note: Club music engineered to the millimetre and then bent out of shape on purpose.

albums.title: Sceneries Not Songs, Volume One
albums.label: Black Market
albums.note: Deep house at its most patient, made by the man who named the genre.

albums.title: Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires
albums.label: Greensleeves
albums.note: The best-titled record in dub and one of the best-mixed, which is a rare combination.

albums.title: The Tired Sounds of Stars of the Lid
albums.label: Kranky
albums.note: Two hours of guitar drone arranged like chamber music, and not one wasted minute.

albums.title: Opal
albums.label: Timedance
albums.note: Bristol bass at its most abstract, with the swing still intact underneath.

albums.title: Big Soup
albums.label: Mo Wax
albums.note: Breakbeats and jazz samples made by someone who clearly finds all of this hilarious.

albums.title: Vantage Isle Sessions
albums.label: Soma
albums.note: Detroit dub techno recorded like a field trip, all rain and distant chords.
albums.why: Detroit dub techno recorded like a field trip, all rain and distant chords. You have 452 plays of Deepchord and skip them 8% of the time, which for a record this slow is devotion, and Dub Chamber is 684.2 hours of your life anyway. Pitchfork gave it 7.6; you will give it a whole evening.

albums.title: Rigning
albums.label: Sending Orbs
albums.note: Icelandic dub techno named after rain, and it does sound exactly like that.
albums.why: Icelandic dub techno named after rain, and it does sound exactly like that. You have 341 plays of Yagya already and skip them 9% of the time, so this is not a leap, it is the record you should have started with. Dub Chamber runs 684.2 hours in your listening; this is the one to hear front to back.

critics.title: BCD
critics.note: The plates the whole lane descends from, and still the cleanest low end ever pressed.

critics.title: Waveform Transmission Vol. 1
critics.note: Detroit techno with nothing decorative left on it, and faster than most things made since.

critics.title: Neptune's Lair
critics.note: Detroit electro built on an underwater mythology, machine funk deep enough to carry it.

critics.title: Modus Operandi
critics.note: Drum and bass engineered like architecture, and the record that taught the genre restraint.

critics.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
critics.note: The mixing desk as lead instrument, and the record every dub producer measures against.

critics.title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92
critics.note: The early Aphex collection where ambient still had a pulse, warm tape-worn melodies over quiet drum machines.

critics.title: Alien
critics.note: Larry Heard in science fiction mode, long synth pieces drifting well away from the dance floor.

critics.title: Incunabula
critics.note: The politest Autechre record, which makes it the one you can actually put on.

critics.title: Timeless
critics.note: Jungle scaled up to orchestral length without losing the break science underneath.

critics.title: Parallel Dimensions
critics.note: House mixed like a jazz record, deliberately rough, and it has aged into a classic.

critics.title: Untrue
critics.note: Pirate radio memory turned into its own genre, rained-on garage and pitched vocal ghosts.

critics.title: Gas
critics.note: Voigt's forest ambient in its first form, strings looped into fog with a kick buried somewhere beneath.

critics.title: Revolution for Change
critics.note: Detroit techno as an actual political position, and the music backs it up.

critics.title: Deep Space
critics.note: Juan Atkins stretching Detroit electro into slow orbit, machine funk with the cabin lights dimmed.

critics.title: East of the River Nile
critics.note: Melodica over dub plates, which should not work and turns out to be sublime.

critics.title: Hazyville
critics.note: House heard through several closed doors, and the blur was already the whole point on this debut.

critics.title: The Deepest Cut Vol. 1
critics.note: Moving Shadow jungle with piano and choir stabs, rollers built more for release than menace.

critics.title: Alcachofa
critics.note: Minimal house that keeps going long past where it should and earns every minute.

critics.title: Silentintroduction
critics.note: Detroit house assembled from loose soul loops and room noise, swinging harder for being left rough.

critics.title: Soul Music
critics.note: Pirate radio nostalgia made by someone who was actually there, which is why it stings.

critics.title: Various: We Are Reasonable People
critics.note: A survey of the Basic Channel offshoot sound: concrete, hiss, and chords arriving like weather fronts.

critics.title: Escape
critics.note: Modern jungle with old-school cuts and none of the nostalgia, breaks handled like precision tools.

critics.title: Midtown 120 Blues
critics.note: Deep house with an essay attached, and both halves are essential.

critics.title: Trilogie de la Mort
critics.note: Hours of ARP synthesizer moving slower than perception, drone as devotional practice.

critics.title: Underwater Dancehall
critics.note: Bristol dubstep stretched to album length, halftime pressure with vocalists given real room.

critics.title: Energique
critics.note: Piano stabs and hoover bass with chart ambitions and warehouse manners.

critics.title: Heavyweight Dub Champion
critics.note: The young engineer proving himself at the desk, drums and bass carved down to outlines while the reverb does the rest.

critics.title: Wet Will Always Dry
critics.note: Techno made from sounds that should not be musical, arranged with total confidence.

critics.title: Trionisphere
critics.note: Kerri Chandler doing what he always does: drums that feel hand-played and chords that feel like church.

critics.title: Blinks
critics.note: Glassy club constructions from the Swedish end of the map, melody kept sharp enough to cut.

critics.title: Controlled Developments
critics.note: St Albans darkness, drum edits engineered to the millimetre under atmospheres borrowed from thrillers.

critics.title: Permafrost
critics.note: Drone recorded as if from inside a glacier, and the most physically cold record here.

critics.title: Mala in Cuba
critics.note: Halftime pressure rebuilt around live Cuban players, and the sub survives the trip intact.

critics.title: United Acid Emirates
critics.note: Acid boxes pushed toward actual songwriting, humour left in and the melodies doing real work.

critics.title: Super Ape
critics.note: The Black Ark at full strength, and the strangest-sounding great record in reggae.

critics.title: Bring
critics.note: Percussion-first techno from a producer who treats every drum hit like a lead line.

critics.title: For Those of You Who Have Never (And Also Those Who Have)
critics.note: Ambient made from worn loops and left unresolved, the kind of record that changes what you reach for at night.

critics.title: Shadows in Blue
critics.note: Bristol techno with the low end doing the storytelling, club tools that hold up far from the club.

critics.title: Cybotron
critics.note: Low end from the man who later built a sound system just to reproduce it properly.

singles.title: Cyan
singles.note: Berlin dub techno with field-recording air in it, chords surfacing and sinking for minutes at a time.

singles.title: Pattern 1
singles.note: The Basic Channel players in a room together, improvising the same idea slowly.

singles.title: Port Gentil
singles.note: Hamburg dub techno that sounds like machinery in a flooded room

singles.title: Distant Transmission
singles.note: Texas electro slowed until it behaves like weather over water.

singles.title: Relish
singles.note: Chain Reaction minimalism from DJ Pete, built from hiss, patience, and very little else.

singles.title: Emerge
singles.note: The same Berlin desk, the same room, a slightly different set of hands.

singles.title: Lyot
singles.note: One chord given a whole side to decay, and it earns every second of it.

singles.title: Seconds to Forever
singles.note: Twelve minutes that change almost nothing, and the almost is the point.

singles.title: M4
singles.note: The Berlin series at its deepest, a groove that never peaks because it never needs one.

singles.title: Minimalism
singles.note: Detroit stripped back until only the ghost of the groove is left standing.

singles.title: Won't Let Go
singles.note: Sweet-toned jungle from the Dutch school, chopped amens under an actual song.

singles.title: Brown Paper Bag
singles.note: An upright bass line and a break, and it won the Mercury with almost nothing else.

singles.title: Rush Hour
singles.note: Golden-era jungle manners with modern low end, rolling rather than ravey.

singles.title: Warhead
singles.note: Bristol drum and bass with a horn stab that has never stopped being borrowed.

singles.title: Jungle Teknah
singles.note: Jungle pushed up to footwork tempo and kept musical the whole way.

singles.title: Mystic
singles.note: Liquid drum and bass made by someone who clearly listens to a lot of soul records.

singles.title: Chopper
singles.note: Rude, warped bass music from Atlanta, drum programming that changes its mind mid-bar.

singles.title: Baianá
singles.note: A Brazilian folk sample cut over a break, and it should not work as well as it does.

singles.title: Forsaken
singles.note: Deep drum and bass in the Photek tradition, every element placed and nothing wasted.

singles.title: Music
singles.note: The record that proved jungle could be pretty without getting soft.

singles.title: Vertigo
singles.note: Bristol dub weight at half speed, with more space in it than anything else here

singles.title: Late Night Blues
singles.note: Bristol at its most patient, where the drop is a suggestion rather than an event.

singles.title: Not Stochastic
singles.note: Bristol drums that lurch without ever falling over, weight and mischief in equal measure.

singles.title: Digidesign
singles.note: Purple synths over dubstep weight, and nobody has copied it properly since.

singles.title: Ramos
singles.note: Tumbling percussion with a hook buried in the toms, made for a dark room and a good system.

singles.title: Blood on My Hands
singles.note: Percussion that circles rather than repeats, and a low end you feel before you hear.

singles.title: Blush
singles.note: The gentle end of Bristol bass, melody first with the sub as a cushion.

singles.title: Anti War Dub
singles.note: Half the frequencies of a normal record and twice the room.

singles.title: Beacon
singles.note: Halftime pressure with real swing, every tone tuned until it hums.

singles.title: Feelin
singles.note: Chicago footwork at full tempo, and the drums are doing something closer to speech.

singles.title: Sex With the Machines
singles.note: German electro at its most severe, vocoder cold and proud of it.

singles.title: Clear
singles.note: Detroit before techno had a name for itself, and the blueprint is all here.

singles.title: Nyctalopia
singles.note: French electro in the Drexciyan shadow, analogue dread with a neon melody on top.

singles.title: No UFO's
singles.note: Juan Atkins on his own, sounding like a transmission rather than a record.

singles.title: Sworn to Secrecy
singles.note: Hamburg electro played off hardware with the levels pushed too far, deliberately

singles.title: Egypt, Egypt
singles.note: One drum machine, one vocoder, and a whole Los Angeles scene downstream of it.

singles.title: Corrosive
singles.note: Modern electro built for big rooms, crunchy machines and no hesitation.

singles.title: Wireless Internet
singles.note: The Drexciya lineage writing about infrastructure and meaning every word.

singles.title: Retina
singles.note: Carl Finlow under another name, small precise melodies over immaculate machine funk.

singles.title: Disco Rout
singles.note: Dutch, cheap, and warmer than any of the gear should allow.

singles.title: Emley Lights Us Moor
singles.note: Voice and bass pulled apart and reassembled, West Yorkshire made strange.

singles.title: Thievery
singles.note: Rhythm treated as something to be broken and then reassembled badly on purpose.

singles.title: Not So Sure
singles.note: Bruised vocals over dissolving club rhythm, tenderness where this music usually wears armour.

singles.title: AS Chingy
singles.note: Club music assembled out of alarm sounds, and it does actually work on a floor.

singles.title: Naughty Dog
singles.note: Deadpan vocals over stripped club drums, menace managed with almost nothing.

singles.title: Hunted
singles.note: Berlin by way of Texas, and the percussion is closer to a threat than a groove.

singles.title: Turbo Rush
singles.note: Industrial texture with a dancer's timing, club music that keeps its elbows out.

singles.title: BIPP
singles.note: Every sound built from scratch, and the whole decade of pop that followed heard it.

singles.title: Middle Ground
singles.note: Raw hardware sketches with the immediacy of a voice memo, rhythm treated as an open question.

singles.title: Volcano
singles.note: Harp, autotune and a drum programme that keeps changing its mind.

singles.title: Sound Surface
singles.note: Loop techno from a lifer, one idea machined until it shines.

singles.title: Grey Fades to Green
singles.note: Madrid techno with the lights off and no interest in a release.

singles.title: Blood Witness
singles.note: Birmingham techno stripped to its bones, and the reverb is the only melody

singles.title: Deathvox
singles.note: Industrial weight without the cosplay, and it moves faster than it sounds.

singles.title: Stowaway
singles.note: British industrial techno with dirt under its nails, distortion doing rhythm-section work.

singles.title: Fear Paralysis
singles.note: Built for the fourth hour of a night rather than the first.

singles.title: Fill Twelve
singles.note: Techno with mangled vocal matter in the drums, tough from a distance and detailed up close.

singles.title: The Bells
singles.note: One riff, no development, and thirty years of floors that still stop for it.

singles.title: Reflection
singles.note: Stripped club techno that trusts the kick and the room to do the work.

singles.title: Your Mind
singles.note: Swedish functionalism, engineered so cleanly it barely sounds like effort.

singles.title: Sirius
singles.note: Chicago house with real jazz in the keys, warm without going soft.

singles.title: Move Your Body
singles.note: The piano house record, made on borrowed gear in a Chicago bedroom.

singles.title: Can You Feel It
singles.note: House that feels handed down rather than produced, gospel implied in every chord.

singles.title: Flash
singles.note: A Chicago record about a nightclub, narrated deadpan over a rhythm that never lets up.

singles.title: Altered States
singles.note: Chicago house that runs eleven minutes and needs every one of them

singles.title: New For U
singles.note: A string loop and a kick, released on his own label, and it went everywhere.

singles.title: Mortal Thoughts
singles.note: Raw Chicago tracking with more soul than polish, the good kind of unfinished.

singles.title: Kaychunk
singles.note: Detroit swing from someone who was still a teenager when he cut it.

singles.title: Love's Got Me High
singles.note: Detroit gospel house with the piano out front, joy played completely straight.

singles.title: Your Love
singles.note: The record the word house was more or less invented to describe.

singles.title: Dub Fever
singles.note: From the engineer behind the African Dub series, drums and echo treated as the whole arrangement.

singles.title: Skylarking
singles.note: That voice over a rhythm with most of the furniture removed.

singles.title: Blood Brothers
singles.note: The dark prince of dub, and this is the most haunted thing in the catalogue

singles.title: Marcus Garvey
singles.note: Roots reggae as history lesson, and the horns carry the argument.

singles.title: Conquering Lion
singles.note: Deep roots severity, a vocal that sounds carved rather than sung.

singles.title: Fisherman
singles.note: Recorded at the Black Ark with the tape running hot and the room half falling apart.

singles.title: Head of the Buffalo Soldier
singles.note: That granite voice over a slow rhythm, half sermon and half growl.

singles.title: Roots and Culture
singles.note: A radio DJ who learned the desk and then out-engineered most of the engineers.

singles.title: Rockers Almighty Dub
singles.note: The Skatalites saxophonist deep in the rockers era, horns floating over a rhythm stripped for parts.

singles.title: Dread Are the Controller
singles.note: Vocal and version on one side, and the version is the better half.

singles.title: Silt
singles.note: Two producers building one seamless hour, and it never once announces itself

singles.title: Kobresia
singles.note: Recorded above the Arctic Circle and it does not let you forget that.

singles.title: Device Control
singles.note: The photographer's music turns out to be all texture and dry wit, gadget-speak recited over a machine pulse.

singles.title: Container Ships
singles.note: A slow harmonic drift with a pulse buried in it, which is exactly your tolerance.

singles.title: Sacer Boreas
singles.note: Pipe organ tuned to make the room itself resonate, and it is genuinely physical

singles.title: Hiatus
singles.note: Guitar processed past recognition and then given somewhere enormous to sit.

singles.title: Chorus Scene
singles.note: Organ tones held until they start to breathe, drone with early-music manners.

singles.title: Heavy Water/I'd Rather Be Sleeping
singles.note: A piano, a voice, and a tape hiss doing as much work as either.

singles.title: Vestiges of an Inheritance
singles.note: Soft loops that barely move and never bore, ambient made for rooms at dusk.

singles.title: Raum
singles.note: A broken filter pedal turned into an entire discography, and this is the best of it.

singles.title: Rev8617
singles.note: Breakbeats and grey ambience in the same track, from the most reliable producer in Munich

singles.title: Out to Rust
singles.note: Clarinet in a techno record, handled so casually you almost miss it.

singles.title: Bby
singles.note: Chopped vocals turned into the hook itself, rave euphoria at a house tempo.

singles.title: Workaround Two
singles.note: Every sound placed on a grid and given room to be heard alone.

singles.title: You Could Be
singles.note: Garage sunshine with a proper vocal on top, club music that grins at you.

singles.title: home
singles.note: Anonymous, playful, and put together with a total disregard for what a club track does.

singles.title: Balance
singles.note: Greyscale drum and bass from Bristol, techno weight moved at jungle speed.

singles.title: Bug Thief
singles.note: Cartoon speed and detail, arranged with far more care than the surface suggests.

singles.title: Blue Violet
singles.note: Half ambient record and half drum workout, switching without warning and earning both

singles.title: Skater's World
singles.note: London weight with all the obvious edges filed off it.

singles.title: Tenacity
singles.note: Rave breaks with real feeling in the pads, memory music that still moves forward.

singles.title: Trip II the Moon
singles.note: Hardcore at its most cheerfully unhinged, and the breakdown is a genuine event.

singles.title: The Sky Was Pink
singles.note: Melodic overload from the Border Community years, synths blooming until they distort.

singles.title: Charly
singles.note: A public information film sampled into a rave record, and it went top three.

singles.title: Raving I'm Raving
singles.note: A sampled piano hook, an injunction from the original writer, and a number two single anyway.

singles.title: Activ 8
singles.note: Dust masks, a Stafford warehouse, and one of the loudest records of its year.

singles.title: Wasted Days
singles.note: Bristol junglism with dancehall in its accent, breaks cut sharp and cheeky.

singles.title: Let Me Be Your Fantasy
singles.note: A rave anthem that waited two years and then went to number one anyway.

singles.title: Sweet Harmony
singles.note: One of the few rave records that is genuinely about joy rather than pressure.

singles.title: On a Ragga Tip
singles.note: The exact moment hardcore and ragga stopped being separate rooms.

singles.title: The Traveller
singles.note: Berlin techno with hardcore memory in its bones, rough breaks under serious chords.
singles.why: Berlin techno with hardcore memory in its bones, rough breaks under serious chords. It sits one room over from Yagya, who you have played 341 times, and it is the louder room.

singles.title: Making Room
singles.note: Berlin patience from someone who was in the room when this sound was decided.
singles.why: Berlin patience from someone who was in the room when this sound was decided. Your 27.4 hours of Yagya are the same patience, a decade downstream.

singles.title: Cellar Door
singles.note: Nantes bass music with the low end hollowed out and the drums left to do the talking, an early single that already had the shape.
singles.why: Nantes bass music with the low end hollowed out and the drums left to do the talking, an early single that already had the shape. The door is Livity Sound: 24.3 hours of the label in your listening, 5 of its artists you play, and Simo Cell has 6 releases there you have never opened.

singles.title: Open Door
singles.note: One loop, nine minutes, and the edit is the entire composition.
singles.why: One loop, nine minutes, and the edit is the entire composition. If DJ Sprinkles is worth 214 plays to you at an 8% skip rate, you already have the attention span this asks for.

singles.title: Silent State
singles.note: Hazy loop techno pressed out of static, music that sounds found rather than made.
singles.why: Hazy loop techno pressed out of static, music that sounds found rather than made. Deepchord is 38.6 hours of your listening, and this is the same weather from a farmhouse in Bavaria.

singles.title: Beau Mot Plage
singles.note: Microhouse with a guitar figure that has outlived the genre name.
singles.why: Microhouse with a guitar figure that has outlived the genre name. It shares a chord sense with Larry Heard, who you have played 588 times and almost never skip.

singles.title: Xine
singles.note: Delicate deep house in the Heard lineage, piano touch and no wasted gestures.
singles.why: Delicate deep house in the Heard lineage, piano touch and no wasted gestures. Your 41.6 hours of Larry Heard are the reason this is here, and it will not embarrass them.

singles.title: Dexter
singles.note: Percussion that behaves like a conversation between people who dislike each other.
singles.why: Percussion that behaves like a conversation between people who dislike each other. Donato Dozzy, 398 plays deep on your shelf, is the nearest thing you own to this kind of nerve.

singles.title: Beyond the Machine
singles.note: Warm, unhurried deep house from Heidelberg, played more than programmed.
singles.why: Warm, unhurried deep house from Heidelberg, played more than programmed. It comes through DJ Sprinkles, 21.2 hours of your listening, and it has the same refusal to hurry.

singles.title: The Splendour
singles.note: Bells used as a rhythm section, and it should be twee and somehow is not.
singles.why: Bells used as a rhythm section, and it should be twee and somehow is not. Fluxion is the anchor, 284 plays of it, and this is the brighter end of the same dub techno idea.

singles.title: I Wanna Go Bang
singles.note: Icelandic rave mischief, one vocal loop over a mean machine groove.
singles.why: Icelandic rave mischief, one vocal loop over a mean machine groove. You have played Aphex Twin 782 times, and this is the same grin with a Reykjavik accent.

singles.title: Theory of Machines
singles.note: Made in Reykjavik and built to sound like something structural failing slowly.
singles.why: Made in Reykjavik and built to sound like something structural failing slowly. Thomas Köner is the anchor, 22.4 hours of him on your shelf, and this is his cold with a pulse in it.

singles.title: Captagon
singles.note: Dub techno recorded in the wettest possible room, and the reverb never fully clears
singles.why: Dub techno recorded in the wettest possible room, and the reverb never fully clears. It is the Deepchord producer under his own name, and you have given Deepchord 452 plays, so the room will feel familiar.

singles.title: Odi et Amo
singles.note: Strings and a vocoder reading Latin, from the other end of the same island.
singles.why: Strings and a vocoder reading Latin, from the other end of the same island. Your 18.6 hours of Eliane Radigue say you can sit still for this.

singles.title: Cameltoe
singles.note: Dutch braindance at its sweetest, toy-box melody over gently broken drums.
singles.why: Dutch braindance at its sweetest, toy-box melody over gently broken drums. DMX Krew is 428 plays deep in your record; this is the same machinery in a better mood.

singles.title: Hubble
singles.note: Everything sounds like it was recovered from a corrupted drive, deliberately.
singles.why: Everything sounds like it was recovered from a corrupted drive, deliberately. Objekt, 468 plays and a 16% skip rate, is the closest neighbour, and this is stranger still.

singles.title: The First Day
singles.note: One idea held for twenty minutes with total conviction, which is the whole appeal
singles.why: One idea held for twenty minutes with total conviction, which is the whole appeal. Gas is 58.4 hours of your listening and you skip it 6% of the time; this asks for the same trust.

singles.title: Forest of Evil
singles.note: Two record collectors building dread out of other people's tape.
singles.why: Two record collectors building dread out of other people's tape. Huerco S. is the anchor at 342 plays, the hiss without the horror.

singles.title: Numb
singles.note: Manchester murk at half speed, a voice suspended in tape sludge.
singles.why: Manchester murk at half speed, a voice suspended in tape sludge. Vladislav Delay, 41.8 hours on your shelf, is the same swamp from the Finnish side.

singles.title: Bone Sucka
singles.note: One of the Hessle founders on his own label, a rude little vocal chop over drums that never resolve into a straight beat.
singles.why: One of the Hessle founders on his own label, a rude little vocal chop over drums that never resolve into a straight beat. Hessle Audio is 31.8 hours of your listening across 7 of its artists, and Pangaea has 4 releases there you have never opened.

mixes.note: The most trusted selector in the country, moving between decades without a seam
Sherelle doing what she does, jungle and footwork at full sprint with the joy left in.
Tim Reaper treating jungle as a living style rather than an archive, new dubs cut in the old grammar.
Pinch keeping Bristol's low end honest, dubplate weight with the patience to let tunes play out.
Bristol dub weight played at half speed, with room to breathe between every record
DJ Python drifting through the ambient end of his record bag, dembow softened into weather.
Helena Hauff at her most direct, electro and acid played loud and unsentimental.
A producer with perfect technical control choosing to make the mix feel unstable
Aya pulling club music apart in real time, funny and rude and precise about it.
Kessler moving between broken drums and straight techno weight without dropping the thread.
Detroit records played by the man who lives there, with all the talking left in
Bradley Zero in collector mode, deep house sequenced with a host's instincts.
Scientist at the controls again, classic rhythms rebuilt live with the echo doing the talking.
Carlos Niño's cosmic Los Angeles hour, percussion and chimes scattered over long ambient light.
A composer playing the drone records that taught her, which is the most useful kind of show
Anz mixing bright and quick, garage and bass records stacked with no dead air.
Skee Mask deep in the ambient and dub end of his collection, breaks kept soft and half buried.
Sam Binga rolling through modern jungle with a Bristol accent, halftime detours included.
Pirate radio recreated by someone who was actually on it the first time
Batu road-testing the new Bristol grammar, drums first and always swinging.
Surgeon mixing like the room is full, hard techno handled with an improviser's ear.
Eris Drew's ecstatic house history lesson, breakbeats and piano and open-hearted mixing.
Swamp dub and forest noise from the Bristol label that treats a riddim as a place to get lost. Rhythm & Sound is the reference point, everything else is further out.
mixes.why: Jack Sapsed's monthly hour of sideways sounds on NTS, this one leaning hard into steppers and dub, Iration Steppas to Jonah Dan. Twelve tracks, 3 by artists you play and 9 you have never heard, and Augustus Pablo, 296 plays on your shelf, is the bridge.

mixes.note: Martelo joining the dots between grime, funky and garage at speed, the whole UK lineage in one sitting. Pinch is where your shelf meets it.
mixes.why: Martelo joining the dots between grime, garage and whatever came out this week, El-B next to TSVI. Fifteen tracks, 4 by names you play and 11 you do not, and Pinch at 812 plays is where your shelf meets it.

mixes.note: Two hours of jungle revival from the crew that made it a party again, chopped breaks and dub pressure all the way down. Tim Reaper is the door this came through.
mixes.why: Two hours of jungle revival from the crew that made it a party again, chopped breaks and dub pressure all the way down. 40 tracks, 9 by artists you already play and 31 you have never heard, and Tim Reaper at 618 plays is the door this came through.

mixes.note: Seattle's long-running reggae programme, deep in the roots and versions end of the record shop. King Tubby is the name you know; the rest were mixed in his shadow.
mixes.why: Kid Hops on KEXP's Saturday reggae programme, Horace Andy and Burning Spear next to this year's dancehall. 54 tracks, 10 by artists you play and 44 you have never heard, with King Tubby's 428 plays as the foothold.

revivals.title: Krautrock
revivals.note: Played into the ground one spring and then dropped along with the whole lane

revivals.title: Dumpster
revivals.note: The nastiest cut on The Power and the Glory, all grind and intent, waiting where you left it.

revivals.title: Getting Me Down
revivals.note: Blawan bending a pop vocal around that lurching kick, and you have left it alone for ages.

revivals.title: Phylyps Trak
revivals.note: Foundation Berlin dub techno, the chord stab a whole genre keeps trying to find again.

revivals.title: Never Tell You
revivals.note: One of the most-played things in the whole record, and silent for two years

revivals.title: Kuula
revivals.note: Dub techno dissolved into mist on Multila, and it has drifted out of your nights.

revivals.title: Ni Ten Ichi Ryu
revivals.note: The most-played drum pattern in your entire record, and untouched for two years

revivals.title: Inner City Life
revivals.note: Diane Charlemagne's voice over rolling breaks, still the emotional centre of the whole style.

revivals.title: The Angels Fell
revivals.note: Blade Runner atmosphere over surgical breaks, and it has gone quiet in your listening.

revivals.title: Qawwali
revivals.note: The dubstep track that still sounds like nothing else, and you stopped playing it

revivals.title: Changes
revivals.note: That melancholy little melody over halftime sway, one of the most tender things dubstep produced.

revivals.title: Mud
revivals.note: Halfstep reduced to bass and menace, still the blueprint.

revivals.title: Bubble Metropolis
revivals.note: Aquatic electro transmissions at their most vivid, and you have stayed on dry land lately.

revivals.title: Xtal
revivals.note: Worn smooth from repetition and then set down completely

revivals.title: You Can't Hide Your Love
revivals.note: Rephlex synth-pop played completely sincere, a love song from the machines.

revivals.title: Pop 1
revivals.note: An hour-long track played twice a week for a year, and then not once since

revivals.title: Requiem for Dying Mothers
revivals.note: Played on repeat through one difficult winter and not since it ended

revivals.title: A Sea of Love
revivals.note: Huerco S. ambient that moves like heat haze, and it has slipped out of your evenings.

revivals.title: Can You Feel It
revivals.note: The record the whole lane rests on, and it has been sitting untouched for a year

revivals.title: Overyohead
revivals.note: Theo Parrish house at walking pace, rough edges kept in because they are the point.

revivals.title: I Can't Kick This Feelin
revivals.note: Detroit house that loops one confession until it becomes a place to live.

revivals.title: Rain
revivals.note: A deep house record about weather that got played through an entire wet spring

revivals.title: Dub Fi Gwan
revivals.note: Tubby's desk in full flight, a rhythm dismantled and rebuilt before it can land.

revivals.title: Your Teeth in My Neck
revivals.note: Horror-titled, sweet-natured dub from the vampire album, the Radics rhythm carrying it easy.

revivals.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
revivals.note: Melodica and echo in perfect balance, still the version most people mean when they say dub.

revivals.title: Ganzfeld
revivals.note: Objekt engineering at its most spacious, a track that seems to rewire the room around it.

revivals.title: Cinderella
revivals.note: Glass-edged club minimalism, pretty and unsettling at once.

revivals.title: Elegant and Never Tiring
revivals.note: Kickless trance euphoria held under glass, rave stabs with nowhere to land.

revivals.title: Lolita
revivals.note: Wore this out over one winter of late trains and has not gone back to it

revivals.title: Vibert Rides Again
revivals.note: Vibert doing what only he does, acid and breaks and a grin you can hear.

revivals.title: Playing With Knives
revivals.note: The rave piano anthem itself, still unreasonably effective.

revivals.title: Metallic Rain
revivals.note: Played constantly while the jungle habit was forming, then dropped once it settled

revivals.title: Swandive
revivals.note: Sully at his most weightless, breaks that fall and keep falling.

revivals.title: Marlow
revivals.note: Bristol drum science with the low end implied as much as played, and you have let it lapse.

revivals.title: Roll With the Punches
revivals.note: Bristol drums at their most patient, and a track you used to open everything with

revivals.title: Shuffle Good
revivals.note: Blunt Bristol drums, function raised to the level of style.

revivals.title: Vantage Isle
revivals.note: Detroit dub techno thick as lake fog, chords looping somewhere below visibility.

revivals.title: Snowflake 1
revivals.note: Icelandic dub techno soft as weather, snowfall looped into rhythm.

revivals.title: Menta
revivals.note: Dozzy hypnosis in miniature, one pattern breathing for as long as you let it.

releases.title: Chalk Line
releases.note: Objekt releases rarely and it is always worth stopping for.

releases.title: Cosmic Void
releases.note: A full jungle album rather than a plate, which he almost never does.

releases.title: Rakka III
releases.note: Uploaded without warning, as always, and worth clearing an evening for.

releases.title: Loos in Twos
releases.note: Kowton in club-tool mode, blunt drum funk that does its job and leaves.

releases.title: Foam
releases.note: Ambient assembled from offcuts, and the seams are the best part.

releases.title: The Head as Form'd in the Crier's Choir
releases.note: Köner builds cold you can stand inside, drone as geography more than music.

releases.title: DJ-Kicks
releases.note: A mix rather than a record, and he sequences like nobody else alive.

releases.title: Spaces and Places Vol. 2
releases.note: The last volume was recorded in a different club every night.

releases.title: Gayest Tits
releases.note: Sprinkles' deep house as essay and refuge at once, long mixes that insist the dance floor has politics.

releases.title: Dismantled Into Juice
releases.note: Drums made from sounds that should not be musical at all.

releases.title: The Cut Off
releases.note: Perc's industrial techno still argues with the room, noise shaped until it grooves.

releases.title: Modern Rave
releases.note: Vibert flipping rave nostalgia into new tunes, acid lines with a wink built in.

releases.title: Journey of the Deep Sea Dweller
Blackbox Life Recorder
releases.note: Still finding new corners in the same machines after all this time.

releases.title: Camelot
releases.note: Ceephax acid with its heart on its sleeve, arcade melancholy over boxes pushed hard.

releases.title: See Mi Yah Remixes
releases.note: The Berlin to Kingston axis revisited, one rhythm versioned until it becomes a philosophy.

releases.title: Multila Reissue
releases.note: Multila back within reach, dub techno at its most eroded and underwater.

releases.title: Sleepygirls
releases.note: Yagya's softest mode, dub techno that works as well asleep as awake.

releases.title: Perspectives
releases.note: Dub techno from the quiet end of the Chain Reaction family.

releases.title: Mirrors II
releases.note: Sub bass recorded in another country again, which always suits him.

releases.title: Utility II
releases.note: Kowton back in album mode, grey-toned club functionalism with more warmth than it admits.

releases.title: Form & Function Vol. 3
releases.note: The third volume of remixes, and the first two are canon.

releases.title: Valve Sound System Archive
releases.note: Dillinja cuts built for the sound system he designed himself, bass treated as an engineering discipline.

releases.title: Vanity Project
releases.note: Club music that keeps dissolving before the drop, deliberately.

releases.title: Canone Infinito II
releases.note: Senni's pointillist trance studies continue, all build and no release, and lovelier for it.

releases.title: Dub From the Roots Reissue
releases.note: Remastered from the original tapes for the first time.

releases.title: Rockers Meets King Tubbys
releases.note: Melodica lines over Tubby-treated rhythms, roots and echo in their classic proportions.

releases.title: Kamikaze Dub Reissue
releases.note: Jammy in his dub prime, drums dropped out and slammed back with total confidence.

releases.title: Bring II
releases.note: Randomer doing drum design as dance music, every hit tuned and mean.

releases.title: Gasoline Age Reissue
releases.note: Guitar drone arranged like chamber music, back in print at last.

releases.title: Occam Ocean Vol. 5
releases.note: A new set of Occam pieces, acoustic players holding Radigue's long tones like held breath.

releases.title: Split Tape
releases.note: Objekt in short form, sound design so dense it rewards headphones and the big room equally.

releases.title: Devil's Dance
releases.note: The Bristol dub record everyone has been waiting on.

releases.title: Blush II
releases.note: Hodge on the melodic end of his range, big-room weight with light coming through it.

catalogs.note: A catalogue of twelve records total, and you have somehow only played half of them.
The most important engineer in music, and the albums under his own name are unopened.
The hits get played constantly and the ambient records he loves most get skipped.
An enormous catalogue reduced to the four tracks everyone knows, which is a waste.
Two albums heard and three never opened, and the unheard ones are the strange ones.
You play the twelve-inches and never the albums, which is where he actually stretches out.
Nine long tracks in your listening and the two most recent records untouched.
A lane you burned out on, with the two best records in it never played once.
